title: Scroll Unroll
hook: Unroll the scroll. Find the line hidden at its core.
sub: A synthetic papyrus, rolled almost eight turns tight. A 20-qubit quantum blur plays the damage and scrambles its ink. Flatten it, slide the reading window, and see how much damage a line of Greek survives.
you_control: Unroll the scroll: push the roll on the desk or in the CT slice, the slider, or a pausable 'Unroll it'
Send the archaeologist moth (the reading window) along the sheet: tap the desk or the CT slice, drag the strip, slider, arrow keys
Step through nine blur-v1 damage jobs (slider or the ink-moved bars); flip blurred vs clean ink; view the raw ink layer
Find the hidden Greek line, then share a link to the exact view
qubits_note: Every job: 20 qubits from the engine's documented rule ceil(log2 w)+ceil(log2 h) on the mask disk's 1001x1001 px bounding box (10+10), size 1024 so no downscaling or tiling. The engine does not report a qubit count.
honesty: Synthetic scroll and ink, no real scroll data; blur-v1 ran on Atlas's classical statevector simulator (no QPU) and only stands in for damage; the unwrapping is classical and knows the spiral exactly; this is not the Vesuvius Challenge method.
